characterList.description: A young man with short blonde hair, blue eyes, and fair skin. He wears a blue T-shirt and has a bearded dragon sitting on his shoulder. He is the video's presenter, talking enthusiastically about the new Blender update.
characterList.name: Southern Shotty

content_metadata.description: Analysis of the video review for the Blender 3.2 update, covering character details, scene breakdowns, storylines, and improvements.

qAndA.answer: Shadow Caustics can be used to create realistic underwater light effects or eye caustics.
qAndA.question: What is one example of how Shadow Caustics can be used in Blender 3.2?

qAndA.answer: Sculpt Paint mode offers existing sculpting tools like masking and blending options, making it more versatile. It's also much faster and capable of handling millions of polygons.
qAndA.question: How does the new 'Sculpt Paint' mode improve upon existing tools?

qAndA.answer: WebP images provide faster saving and smaller file sizes compared to PNGs, improving workflow efficiency.
qAndA.question: What's the benefit of using WebP images in Blender?

qAndA.answer: You can now name, lock, and mute individual channels in the Video Sequencer, making it easier to manage complex projects.
qAndA.question: What are some usability improvements made to the Video Sequencer?

qAndA.answer: Proxies were removed because the 'Library Override' feature now provides a more flexible and powerful solution for handling complex animations.
qAndA.question: Why were 'Proxies' removed from the animation system?

timecoded_text_to_speech.text: Hi, I'm Southern Chaudy, and today we have a new Belender 3.2 update, which means we're
going to go through all the new features in less than five minutes.
With that being said, let's get started.
Along requested features finally here, we have Light Groups and Cycles.
This allows you to group collections of lights to use in Lighting Passive.
This opens up a ton of creative potential for Lighting artists in the Composer.
We now have true shadow costics in Belender.
Example uses are Underwater Costics and Eye Costics.
This is based on Manifold Next Event Estimation, a method developed for production rendering
where precision and performance are important.
It's intended to be used on few selected objects in your scene, and this first implementation
has some technical limitations such as no reflective costics, and check out these release notes
for more details.
Another big addition is Volumes Now Support Motion Blur.
It works by using the Speed Attributes from Volumes Made in Blender or External Open
VDB Files in Ported From Other Software.
AMD GPU Rendering is now supported on Linux for RDNA and RDNA2 graphic cards.
You can override color management settings on the render output now.
Some other changes include support using Adaptive Sampling with Scramble Distance, Alpha
Outputs on the Objective Pinot, and finally, you can now bake two Udium tiles.
Apparently being the cool sculpting tool in Blender wasn't enough because now you can
paint in sculpt mode, with existing tools such as the various massing options this makes
it an advantageous option.
The painting mode is now much faster and able to handle up to millions of polygons plus
new tools to modulate wet paint.
There's a smear brush, color filters to modify existing colors, and you can mask by colors.
Vertex colors are now called Color Attributes.
They've been refactored into more generic attributes that are faster, play better with geometry
nodes and support A-bit and 32-bit colors in Vertex or Face Corner domains.
Geometry node curves got some hefty improvements across most nodes with some seeing up to 13
times performance boost.
Other nodes have been improved as well, full list in the Releases nodes.
We have a new node called the Duplicate Elements which can duplicate points, edges, faces,
instances, and curves.
Named Attributes are back.
Last scene in Blender 2.93 LTS, support for naming attributes was removed in 3.0 to make
room for the field system.
They are now back as 3 nodes to get, set, and removed named attributes.
The geometry nodes modifier now shows which attributes are used and a new overlay shows
which named attributes are used even inside node groups.
The new faces player node can tell when the triangles of an in-gone don't lie in the
same plane.
There have been many minor adjustments to the UI as well for readability.
We got a cool new grease pencil modifier.
The envelope modifier draws a line between points for a pretty neat sketch like effect.
The dot dash modifier can now cycle the generated strokes.
The build modifier has a new face mode and the smooth modifier can keep shape and got
a much improved smoothing algorithm.
Playback Speed has been improved for grease pencil objects sharing the same data.
We have a new curve pen tool in curve edit mode that can be used to be rapidly edit and
create curves.
You can now apply modifiers on objects, multiple users, as well as applying location, rotation,
or scale, finally addressing a long overdue request by the community.
Select vertices with similar crease values and nerves, curves, knots, generation have been
improved.
Library Overrides saw a big performance boost.
Re-sinking libraries is not over 10 times faster depending on the project.
Re-sinking library overrides is now much easier thanks to the new properties view in the
outliner displaying all overwritten properties at once.
Plus the hierarchy view that shows relationships between properties.
Collection assets are now supported.
An automatic preview image is generated when marking them as an asset.
We got a new experimental OBG importer and anxporter written in C++ which is much faster than
the previous importer.
Blender now supports WebP which is similar to PNG but saves faster and generates smaller
file sizes.
The sequencer continues to be paused with the ability to name channels as well as lock or
mute an entire channel.
Handling of animated strips has also been improved with better filter method on transform
and many more usability improvements.
Virtual reality now supports more view options and HDC Vive focus through controllers.
The GLTFx board has seen huge improvements across the board and has been refactored completely.
FVX now has support for camera depth of field, F curves grouped by bones, and other small
improvements.
Animation has had lots of little user experience quad of life tweaks including discount
and nudie filter, is now available in the dope sheet.
Fake action is available from the edit menu, motion paths now select more sensible frame
ranges by default and provide more options such as selected keyframes or all keyframes.
Markers are easier to select and can be renamed with F2 now, the same way you can rename
NLA strips.
You can enter NLA tweak mode now without disabling all other tracks.
Proxies have been removed for good in this release and Blender will do its best to replace
existing proxies with the much more flexible library override.
ED saw some minor under the hood changes including plugging and a bump without height is
now optimized.
A shader compilation info has been moved to the viewport.
Materials using shader to RGB no longer receive screen space reflections or subsurface scattering
effects and displacement bumps now affects image textures box projection mode.
Figure under the hood changes for EVR plane for the coming releases so be looking forward
to that.
Python exceptions from the tech center are now displayed in the info editor as well as
the usual additions and deprecations in the Python API.
These are a bit too technical to list out so check the notes for exact details.
As usual there are hundreds of bug fixes, minor features and improvements which of course
can be seen at the link in the description below.
If you like what you see go support Blender by joining the development button.
